the Si@c PAN@graphite composite electrode is a promising candidate for anodes of lithium ion batteries.
the Si@c PAN@graphite nanocomposite is a promising anode material for high performance lithium ion batteries.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the core shell Si@c PAN structure can effectively accommodate the large volume change of silicon particles during cycling, and that a graphite matrix can efficiently prevent the aggregation of Si@c PAN nanoparticles and provide an efficient electron transport.

a three dimensional Si@c PAN@graphite nanocomposite structure can be successfully prepared via a simple high energy ball-milling followed by heat treatment, and it shows an excellent electrochemical performance as an anode for lithium-ion batteries.

the Si@c PAN@ G nanocomposite electrode can be a promising candidate for next-generation anodes of lithium ion batteries with a high specific capacity, high rate capability and long cycling performance.
